title: Data Exchange Lifecycle and Integrations
readerIntent: Understand interaction with persistence, search, cache, events, jobs, workflows, and publishing.
priorKnowledge: Understand the import or export definition.
owner: Data exchange orchestration and each integrated capability owner
summary: Data exchange coordinates existing authorities; it does not create alternate database, search, cache, event, workflow, or publishing paths.

sections.heading: Cross-capability behavior
items: Persistence: imports save and exports query through schema services.
Search: import headers may target authorized index services; normal record imports may trigger configured indexing.
Cache: successful changes invalidate or refresh through the owning capability.
Events: finalization may publish bounded facts after authoritative success.
Scheduled jobs: trigger named recurring imports or exports, not arbitrary code or destinations.
Workflows and publishing: stage business changes for approval and publish through their existing contracts.

sections.heading: Consistency
paragraphs: A run defines transaction or batch boundaries, partial-failure policy, retry and idempotency, derived-system lag, reconciliation, and rollback evidence. Search and cache remain derived views; export correctness is based on authorized authoritative contracts.

sections.heading: End-to-end import lifecycle
items: Receive and authenticate source.
Validate metadata, format, checksum, and scope.
Preview or stage normalized records.
Persist through owning services in bounded batches.
Finalize search, cache, events, workflow, and publishing.
Complete with reconciliation and auditable summary.

sections.heading: End-to-end export lifecycle
items: Authorize request and field policy.
Resolve snapshot and query through owners.
Render through the selected format provider.
Deliver through a governed destination.
Record checksum, counts, expiry, and access.
Clean partial or expired artifacts.

sections.heading: Restart and compensation
paragraphs: Runs persist enough identity and progress to distinguish completed, retryable, failed, uncertain, and compensated work. Restart does not assume an in-memory batch is authoritative.
Side effects that cannot join one transaction use idempotency, finalization, reconciliation, and explicit compensation.

sections.heading: No parallel authority
items: No direct database driver calls from a reader or writer.
No raw search-engine bulk path outside the search contract.
No request-selected remote code, URL, credential, processor, topic, or destination.
No separate documentation-content import engine; documentation uses the Nodics content-pack import contract.

sections.heading: Lifecycle evidence
items: Source and destination identity and authorization.
Validated, accepted, rejected, skipped, updated, and created counts.
Batch, transaction, retry, resume, and compensation results.
Index, cache, event, workflow, and publishing finalization.
Checksum, audit, retention, cleanup, and reconciliation.
